newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo, consortium sign deal on JCI sale.
newsitem.headline: Anglo, consortium sign deal on JCI sale.

text.p: Anglo American Corp and African Mining Consortium on Thursday signed an agreement whereby Africa Mining Group would own 34.9 percent of JCI Ltd.

The signing of the agreement follows Anglo American's announcement on November 26 that it had reached agreement in principle with a consortium led by black empowerment group Capital Alliance Holdings Ltd on the sale of its stake in JCI for 54.50 rand per share or 2.88 billion rand.
The purchase would take effect from January 1, 1997, the companies said in a joint statement on Thursday.
An additional 1.3 percent of JCI's issued share capital will be made available through a retail offer to an independent trust set up for members of the black community over a period of four months.
The consortium would have the right of first refusal for a period of five years to purchase the remaining 13 percent stake held by Anglo American and its affiliate De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd.

JCI's board of directors would be reconstituted to comprise 14 members, of whom seven members would be nominated by the consortium, including the chairman, while Anglo American would have certain minority protection rights.
The agreement is subject to the fulfilment of certain suspensive conditions, including a due diligence investigation which will last until February 28 1997.
During this time the consortium would also finalise the funding required for the purchase of the JCI shares.

"We have already started talking to a number of financial institutions, both local and abroad and some of them are very positive," Africa Mining Group chairman Reuel Khosa said. "We have had a very positive reaction."
The consortium was of the opinion that the purchase price represented a discount to the fair value of JCI.
JCI shares closed on Thursday at 47.75 rand.

The consortium includes African Renaissance Holdings, Co-ordinated Network Investments (Pty) Ltd, Corridor Development Corporation, Khotso Investments (Pty) Ltd, Northern Corporate Investment Holdings (Pty) Ltd, Thebe Investment Corp (Pty) Ltd and Women's Development Bank Investment Holdings Ltd.
